title: Six weeks of correspondence: 29 September to 9 November 2026
summary: A dated summary of the project's emails with archives, registries, police, heritage bodies and regulators over six weeks: what was asked, what came back, and what is still open.
body: Between 29 September and 9 November 2026 the project's mailbox exchanged 462 dated emails with 49 public bodies, archives and companies: 222 sent and 240 received. Of the replies, 87 were automatic acknowledgements, 28 stated that the information was not held, 19 asked for clarification or identification, 14 pointed elsewhere, 12 gave part of what was asked, 9 carried disclosures and 8 refused. Every item below is journalled, with its date and source, in the forensic journal.

Land registration. On 4 November 2026 HM Land Registry's Wales Office answered, point by point, a letter of 12 August about the surviving first-registration documents. It gave one concrete answer: the 'no question or doubt' statement sits in the 1982 application for first registration. It declined alteration of the register and indemnity, and named the court as the forum for those questions. A separate EIR and FOI request of 20 October was logged on 23 October as F261029 and F261030, with a reply due by 17 November 2026. A request for the household's own records, logged on 1 October with a 28 October date, was paused on 27 October for identity checks, reset to 6 November, and answered that day in three encrypted parts that have not yet been read.

Police and prosecution. On 6 November 2026 South Wales Police completed internal review 1188/26 of FOI 719/26 and upheld its position that no information is held. A first copy of that review, sent on 26 October, arrived as a password-protected file with no password. FOI 1264/26, on non-personal operational records, was clarified on 13 and 29 October and is still open, with the force warning of a backlog beyond 20 working days. The force answered a personal-records request on 4 November in a protected file; its contents are personal and are not published. On 21 October the Crown Prosecution Service replied that it cannot take evidence directly from the public and pointed to the police.

Heritage bodies. Cadw answered ATISN 26-0009 on 6 November 2026, the twentieth working day. The file on the 6 December 1988 decision not to list Great House Farm is not held. Cadw released five internal documents: an internal email of 1 June 2026 records that the file 'has been destroyed', and a resurvey-database extract of 2007 lists file CL 72/381 with the date 21 January 1993. Its second request, ATISN 26-0141 on movable property from the farm, is logged as received on 29 October with a reply due by 26 November. The Royal Commission replied on 3 November that every record it holds is listed under Coflein site 20182, that three title records of 1926 and 1938 are not held, and that its limit for free searches has been reached. Heneb confirmed on 4 November, for the first time, that both its digital and paper HER files were searched and that all it holds is on Archwilio; it does not hold the 1983 to 1989 planning consultation letters.

Archives and libraries. Glamorgan Archives wrote on 22 October that police occurrence books end in 1984 and station logs in 1979, that the 1988 Weekly Orders exist but are closed because they name serving officers. On 6 November it set out eight record series with estimated search times, judged none likely to hold a 1969 root deed, a 1938 conveyance or a notice to the occupiers, and confirmed the parish vestry records are not held. The National Library of Wales found no further classmarks on 29 October and, on 4 November, refused FOI/2026/16 under section 21, pointing to its reading room. At The National Archives, a request made on 2 September is still unanswered against the Archives' own date of 23 September; internal review CAS-356384 was extended to 20 November and FOI CAS-361652 is due by 13 November.

Maps, water and museums. Ordnance Survey replied on 6 November that it holds no record of who supplied or authorised the name, but sent five map extracts: the house is 'Ty-Mawr' in 1947 and 'Ty Mawr Farm' from between 1965 and 1971. It added that the Object Name Book for sheet ST1673 is recorded at The National Archives as missing at transfer. Dŵr Cymru replied on 6 November that records of the ending of the farm's water supply are not environmental information and, in any case, that 1980s records are past retention and not held. Museum Wales re-ran its searches and on 4 November confirmed nothing is held on the farm's furniture and fittings.

Government and regulators. The Ministry of Defence returned a nil result to a records request on 9 October and relogged a later request as FOI2026/25726, due by 26 November. The Wales Office logged 26FOI 135, also due by 26 November, and DCMS logged FOI2026/11260, due by 18 November. An email to the Cabinet Office correspondence address on 31 October could not be delivered. The Information Commissioner's Office opened complaint IC-586450-N8N0 on 22 October and, on 3 November, case IC-591931-B6H0 for more time to complain about a Museum Wales answer.

Council. On 9 November the Vale of Glamorgan Council's scrutiny officer explained that a topic suggestion now goes through the online form, accepted the earlier wording as the submission, and gave 1 December 2026 as the next agenda it could reach after the Chair's screening.

Still open on 10 November 2026: The National Archives, FOI CAS-361652 due 13 November, internal review due 20 November, and the request of 2 September now overdue. HM Land Registry, F261029 and F261030 due 17 November. DCMS and the Crown Prosecution Service, both due 18 November. The National Library of Wales, FOI2026/17 due 25 November. Cadw ATISN 26-0141, the Ministry of Defence and the Wales Office, all due 26 November. South Wales Police FOI 1264/26, no date given. The council scrutiny topic, 1 December agenda. Two ICO cases, not yet decided. Points not yet answered: what record supports Cadw's 1 June 2026 note, and whether the Royal Commission's reply of 3 November is a formal refusal with a right of review.
